chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: The 'Magsie Evonce' Savoy date in Detroit
summary: Teddy Reig put out a date with Ammons and Leo Parker under McGhee's nickname.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You recorded with him, and I always remember that because you used that pseudonym, or they used it for you, of "Magsie Evonce".
How did that happen? On Savoy.
This was a date that was done in Detroit.

So Teddy Reig, he asked me whether I would mind making the date, and I said, "Sure, I'll be glad to" -- because I was glad to record with anybody during that stage. And we just played the tunes, man. It was such a happy affair, there was no problems, we didn't have no problems, because everybody was playing and everybody could take care of business. And Teddy Reig put the date together, and it turned out a very good date.
Like, Leo Parker had an original chart. And he said, "Maggie, would you make this record with me?" I said, "Oh,
man, don't be funny." So we went on down there and made that date, and it turned out very good.
And you were under contract at that time to Dial?

Teddy Reig always called me "Magsie." He always called me that. So he just said, "I'll put that on the album." I said, "That's all right with me. If you want to use that name, it's all right" -- because soon they'll find out....
Everybody knew who it was anyway.
Yeah, they'd know who it was anyway. So he put it out. But I was on my way out to California when we made that date.
